summary: Build report pages bespoke and with soft-ui, then judge each pair blind for intent match

a_only: A headline sentence that states the answer: net profit $55,637, $20,263 (27%) below budget, with contractors and print resale named as the cause
KPI cards for revenue, gross profit and operating expenses, each with its budget and variance
A section-level build-up waterfall (revenue, cost of sales, gross profit, opex, net) with a dashed budget bar beside each actual bar
A variance bridge from budgeted net profit ($75,900) to actual net profit, one step per account
Text callouts that explain the contractors, print resale, design fees and marketing variances
F/U labels and an inline variance bar column in the P&L statement
Net profit by month as bars coloured above or below budget, plus a cumulative actual-vs-budget net profit line
Small multiples of monthly actual vs budget for the four accounts that move most
A monthly P&L table by section (revenue, cost of sales, gross profit, opex, net) with the variance for each month
b_only: Gross margin (68.2%) and net margin (14.3%) KPI cards
A separate KPI card for budgeted net profit, and a second card for the variance as a percent
An account-level waterfall of actuals only (revenue accounts up, cost accounts down, to net profit), with no budget comparison
A horizontal bar chart of each account's effect on profit
An account-by-month heatmap of the favourable or unfavourable variance, with totals
A second all-accounts table, grouped by section and sorted by effect on profit (this mostly repeats the statement)
Revenue by month as actual vs budget bars
judge.why: A answers the brief's four questions in the order the brief asks them. It gives the net-profit gap first, then shows the build-up and the variance bridge against budget, and its callouts explain the cause. B's build-up waterfall has no budget, its statement signs variance as actual minus budget without F/U labels, and its accounts table repeats the statement, so the owner must work out the story alone.

bespoke.notes: The page opens with the answer: half-year net profit is $55,637, which is $20,263 (27%) below budget, and contractors and print resale explain the gap. Below the headline are four KPI tiles, a waterfall from revenue to net profit (actual against budget), and a bridge from budget net profit to actual net profit by account. Then come the full P&L statement with favourable/unfavourable variance bars, the monthly and cumulative net profit charts, small charts for the four accounts that move most, and a monthly P&L table. All charts are inline SVG with no libraries, and the page has light and dark colour tokens.

error_lines: error data.bridge.sort: no column "['ord', '-net_a']". Columns: ord, section, account, count, net_a
error layout[1].row[0].chart: no dataset "bridge". Datasets: pnl, half, accounts, monthly
tool.friction: 1) The `pct` format expects a value that is already multiplied by 100, but `explain` does not say this. My first render showed a gross margin of "0.7%" (the true value is 68.2%) and table variances such as "0.2%" (the true value is 15.3%). I found this only in the screenshot and fixed it with "100 * ..." in every computed column. The statement component's own % column was correct, so the two formats differ. 2) Dataset `sort` takes one column only, and a list fails. To order the waterfall bars (Revenue first, then Cost of sales, then Operating expenses, each by size), I had to make a composite key "ord * 10000000 - net_a". I also had to repeat the section-sign expression in each `add` column, because an `add` column cannot use another `add` column from the same step. 3) A stat tile cannot take its delta or tone from data. I wanted one "Net profit $55,637" tile with a delta of "-$20,263 / -26.7% vs budget". Instead I made separate tiles from `data`/`col`, and I set `tone: bad` by hand after I saw the value. This hard-codes a judgement that the data does not drive. 4) No stat or tile form takes many values from one data row, so each of the six KPI tiles repeats `data: half, agg: sum, col: ...` on a one-row group that I made from a constant column ("half: 'H1'"). That workaround is not obvious. 5) The heatmap has no `labels` or legend label, so its legend shows the raw column name "sum of fav". 6) The table `group` orders its groups alphabetically (Cost of sales, Revenue, Operating expenses), not in P&L order, and I found no group-order prop. 7) The statement can show only the half-year columns. I wanted a month-by-month statement view as a second tab, but there is no pivot step to turn months into columns. 8) The waterfall builds up by account and has no intermediate Gross profit subtotal bar. The chart's `total` gives only the final bar. 9) The `--shot` screenshot option of `render` was the only way to see the pct bug. "check ok" passed with the wrong numbers. The catalog does not list `--shot`, so I found it only through `render --help`.

a_only: A tab on the forest plot that shows a second forest plot with only the low-bias trials
A box plot of sleep onset by arm in the largest trial
A table grouped by risk of bias: trials, participants, weight % and unweighted mean MD per bias level
Quartile, min and max columns in the arm summary table
A folded Study details panel with the full study table (year, n, CI, weight bars) and the pooled key-value list (model, p, i2, tau2, q_p, grade)
b_only: A headline sentence that states the conclusion (about 10 minutes, holds without the high-bias trials)
A low-bias pooled diamond inside the main forest plot, and sort buttons (weight, year, effect, bias)
Colour-coded bias in the forest plot, and an n column in the forest table
A 'Do the studies agree?' section: an I² gauge on Low to Considerable bands, a statistics table with plain readings, and a 95% prediction interval (-15.5 to -4.1) that B computed itself
A focused sensitivity mini-forest (all 9 vs low-bias only vs the two high-bias trials), with a 1.2 min shift note
Study labels on the scatter, a pooled reference line, a log x axis and a note that 9 trials are too few for a funnel-plot test
A mirrored histogram with the medians marked, a Difference row (-8.4 mean, -8.0 median) and IQR in the arm table
A note that the raw mean difference (-8.4) is not the same as the -7.8 entered in the meta-analysis
A Draft text for the discussion block with a copy button
judge.why: Each page gives the reader a forest plot, effect against sample size and the largest trial's distribution, in the same order. B answers each of the brief's questions directly, in a heading and an annotated view, and for this reader it also adds the agreement section, a direct sensitivity comparison and draft discussion text, while A leaves the reader to draw the conclusions from generic charts and tables.

bespoke.notes: The page opens with the answer: a headline, then 4 key figures (pooled effect, GRADE certainty, I², low-bias-only effect). A forest plot follows, sortable and coloured by risk of bias, with diamonds for the pooled result and the low-bias-only result. Next come two cards side by side, one on heterogeneity (it adds an approximate prediction interval, which I computed and flagged as not in the source files) and one on the bias sensitivity check. Then an effect versus sample-size scatter that shows small-study effects, and a back-to-back histogram with summary table for Hale 2022 (the largest trial). The page ends with draft discussion text that the reader can copy. It also flags that the raw mean difference in Hale 2022 (-8.4 min) differs from the -7.8 min that the meta-analysis uses.

tool.friction:
Both renders printed "check ok" and no "fixed" or "error" lines. The main problem is the pooled result. pooled.json is a single object, and no component can read its numbers. So I copied the pooled values by hand into the spec: -9.8 [-12.4, -7.2], I² 38, τ² 4.1, Q p 0.12, GRADE moderate, and the low-bias-only -8.6 [-10.6, -6.6]. These values appear twice: in the stat tiles and in the forest `pooled:` map. The skill says not to copy data into the spec, but I had no other way.

- **Stat tiles:** a stat with `data` does only count/sum/mean over rows. A single-object file loads as key/value rows, so a tile cannot point at one field, for example `value: pooled.md`.
- **Forest diamond:** `forest.pooled` takes only a literal map. It cannot take a dataset field, for example `pooled: {data: pooled, est: md, lo: ci_low, hi: ci_high}`. The nested `low_bias_only` object needs a path such as `pooled.json#low_bias_only`, and I could not see that this works for an object rather than an array.
- **No weighted mean:** grouping by bias with `mean: [md]` gives an unweighted mean. I labeled that column "mean MD (unweighted)". I could not compute a weight-weighted mean per group without a two-step `add`/`then`, and the docs do not show that.
- **Missing views:** I wanted a funnel plot (MD against standard error, with pseudo-CI lines) to show small-study effects. I used a scatter of MD against n, split by bias, instead. I also could not show a prediction interval on the forest plot, and the data does not include one.
- **Hand-written callout:** a text callout has no way to cite computed counts, such as "8 of 9 CIs exclude zero". I wrote that sentence by hand.
- **Output path:** the docs do not say that `render` takes `-o`. I guessed it, and it worked.

a_only: Headline that states the conclusion (word of mouth and spend drive growth, support strain is the brake)
KPI tiles for churn at month 24 (3.7% vs 4.1%) and support quality at month 24 (0.57 vs 0.46, starts at 0.94)
Loop markers (R1, R2, R3, B1) placed on the diagram, and selecting a loop traces its path
Plain-language description of each loop, as cards next to the diagram
Short note under each chart (for example, the +1,403 gap shaded, and double staff at month 24 equals baseline at month 12)
Loop membership (for example B1 R3) under each column of the influence matrix, plus row and column totals and an outline on each team's strongest cell
Four notes that read the matrix (Support owns the brake, and so on)
A 'For discussion' section with three prompts for leadership
b_only: Lift shown as its own KPI (70.1%)
Text callout that sums up the loops and why doubling staff helps
Separate 'Strongest levers' table (team, variable, strength)
Folded 'Model detail' panel with tabs: a searchable table of causal links with polarity, the variables grouped by type, and the raw simulation rows that can be filtered by scenario
judge.why: Both pages use the same parts in the same order: KPIs, then the causal-loop diagram with the loop list, then three scenario line charts, then the team-by-variable heatmap. Page A suits an offsite better because it tells the leaders what to conclude at each step: the loops are placed on the diagram, each chart and the matrix have notes that read them, and discussion prompts close the page. Page B shows the data with less reading of it, and it hides the raw tables in a folded panel.

bespoke.notes: The page leads with the headline answer and four KPI tiles. Three sections follow. The first is a hand-drawn SVG causal loop diagram that shows polarity badges, stock, flow and auxiliary node styles, and loop markers; clickable loop cards highlight each loop's path. The second is three small-multiple line charts (customers, support quality, churn) that compare the two scenarios, with direct end labels, a shaded gap and a hover readout. The third is a heatmap of team influence that outlines each team's strongest lever and has a short read beside it, followed by discussion takeaways for the offsite.

tool.friction: 1) The pct format multiplies nothing: it expects a value that is already a percent. Fractions such as support_quality 0.78 and churn_rate 0.029 drew as "0.8%" and "0%" on the axes, and the lift stat showed "0.7%". The render check still printed "check ok", so I only caught it on a headless-Chrome screenshot. I fixed it with add: {x_pct: "col * 100"} columns. A fraction-aware format, or a warning when pct values are all below 1, would stop this mistake. 2) In the graph component, `by: type` (boxes for stock, flow and aux) made the causal loop diagram hard to read: the boxes overlapped and the edges crossed through them. I dropped `by` and coloured the nodes with `tone` instead, but the page has no legend for the node colours, so I described them in a note. 3) The graph cannot highlight one feedback loop. A loop `path` is a list of nodes, and no dataset step turns the consecutive pairs of a path into edges, so I could not add a tab for each loop with its edges highlighted. The loops show only as a table with the path as comma text, and the table has no arrows. 4) Edge polarity draws as small +/− glyphs that are hard to read at normal size. 5) The baseline-versus-scenario lift needed a long workaround: a filtered dataset, a rename so the joined columns did not clash, a join and an add. A "pivot" or "spread by scenario" step would make the delta direct. A stat also cannot compute a delta from data, so the two month-24 customer tiles have no delta. 6) I could not show loop polarity (R/B) on the diagram itself, and the graph has no loop markers such as the R1 or B1 labels inside a cycle. 7) The chart and stat tiles cannot be linked to a scenario toggle. I used series on each line chart instead.
